strengths: Novel ESD framework: Signal-aware complexity measure naturally capturing signal-spectrum alignment without restrictive source conditions or eigenvalue decay assumptions
Rigorous minimax theory: Sharp minimax rates (Kσ²) with matched upper/lower bounds via Assouad's method; Theorems 3.2-3.3 establish optimality
Insightful ridge analysis: Section 5 rigorously explains saturation effects, clarifying why ridge-guided complexity measures fail and why ESD is canonical
Generality: Framework applies to arbitrary kernels and extends to linear/RKHS regression without classical assumptions
Gradient flow dynamics: Theorem 6.2 provides rare non-asymptotic analysis showing OP-GF can reduce ESD, with detailed ODE analysis
Comprehensive treatment: 54 pages of careful technical development with complete proofs; clear logical progression from sequence models to extensions
weaknesses: Limited practical applicability: ESD is non-computable from data—requires knowing true signal θ*; no algorithm for kernel selection or adaptation guidance

Restrictive Theorem 6.2 assumptions: Assumption 6.1 with multiple technical conditions specific to proof; only covers eigenvalue learning (fixed eigenfunctions); success probability 1-4/n concerning for large d; artificial initialization b₀

Incremental improvements: Signal-spectrum alignment importance known; PC optimality established; Examples 3.4 show framework mostly recovers classical rates, suggesting results are reframing rather than fundamentally new
Gradient flow gaps: Section 6 limited to eigenvalue learning; Section 10.2 treatment of general eigenfunctions incomplete; Figure 5 experiment doesn't compare against adaptive kernel baselines
RKHS restrictiveness: Assumes eigenfunctions fully known/computable (unrealistic); additional (K,n)-regularity assumption (Assumption 9.4); excludes unbounded targets
Weak experimental validation: Synthetic data only; no comparison to other adaptive methods; no real datasets; confirmatory rather than exploratory experiments

strengths: Novel alignment-sensitive complexity measure (ESD) that captures signal-kernel alignment without requiring source conditions or eigenvalue decay assumptions
Comprehensive theoretical analysis with matching upper and lower bounds across sequence models, linear regression, and RKHS regression
Insightful analysis of why ridge regression cannot define intrinsic complexity (Section 5), with clear differentiation from existing measures (deff(ν), k*)
Sound mathematical development with rigorous proofs and appropriate use of techniques like Assouad's lemma
Clever reduction from RKHS regression to sequence models via Equation (3), simplifying analysis while maintaining rigor
Clear presentation of how ESD recovers classical results (Example 3.4) while enabling analysis of settings where classical framework fails
weaknesses: Limited practical applicability: ESD is a population-level diagnostic that depends on unknown signal f* and cannot be computed without knowing the target. No guidance on algorithmic use beyond theoretical analysis

Theory-practice gap in adaptive learning: Theorem 6.2 (main adaptive result) only shows ESD reduction under restrictive Assumption 6.1, not improved generalization bounds. Analysis covers only eigenvalue learning with fixed eigenfunctions, leaving evolving eigenfunctions for future work—contrary to main motivation

Restrictive and difficult-to-verify assumptions: Assumption 6.1 requires specific signal separation, eigenvalue lower bounds n^{-δ}, and complex ordering conditions (points 1-4 of Theorem 6.2) that are problem-dependent and unlikely to hold broadly

Limited experimental validation: All experiments use synthetic data with controlled misalignment. No real datasets, practical benchmarks, or comparison with competing adaptive methods. Figure 5 uses only 4-layer linear networks

Incomplete treatment of RKHS regression extension: Assumes eigenfunctions are 'fully known and computable' (p. 20), a severe practical limitation that contradicts the motivation of learning representations. This restriction is acknowledged but unresolved

Gap between motivation and results: Paper motivates by claiming to explain why finite-width neural networks with evolving features outperform kernel methods, but only analyzes restricted eigenvalue learning with fixed eigenfunctions
